I am 53 years old, been farming these same fields for 30 years. Never went to school, can't read those papers the county office gives out, but I know this land like my own hands. My wife and me, we are the only ones at home — our son works in Shijiazhuang at a factory, sends some money back but not much. Ten mu is enough to keep us busy but not so big that we need to hire help, which is good because hired labor costs 150 yuan a day now and we can't afford that.

For the winter wheat, I plant the whole ten mu in early October, right after the maize comes off. I buy my wheat seed from the county supply store — I don't save my own seed anymore because after a few years it gets weak and the yield drops. I always put down one bag of compound fertilizer for every two mu before planting, and I run the rotary tiller to work it in. That's what I've always done. Then in late March, when the wheat starts to joint, I walk the fields and look at the color. If it looks yellow and hungry, I topdress with urea — about half a bag per mu. I irrigate three times for wheat: once before winter to help it survive the cold, once at jointing in spring, and once at grain filling. The well water costs electricity money, but wheat is our main food — we need the flour, so I don't skip water on wheat. I spray herbicide once after planting, and if I see aphids in spring, I spray insecticide once. I expect about 400 jin per mu if the weather is fair. Last year was dry and I only got 350, but most years it's around 400.

For the summer maize, the window is tight — sometimes only two or three days between wheat harvest and planting. I buy hybrid maize seed every year from the supply store; you can't save hybrid seed, everyone knows that. I put all the fertilizer in at planting — compound fertilizer in the furrow, about one bag for every two and a half mu, and a handful of urea too. No time for split application, the season is too short. I till once quickly with the rotary machine if the stubble is thick, but if the ground is soft enough I plant right away without tilling — the neighbors do that now and it works fine. I irrigate twice: once right after planting if it's dry, and once at the big trumpet leaf stage. The summer rains usually do the rest. I spray herbicide once and insecticide once for the corn borers. I expect about 450 jin per mu. Two years ago I got 500 jin because the rains were good. I don't gamble on new varieties or fancy methods — at my age, doing what I know is safer than trying something strange and losing a whole season.
